mechanism: Mefloquine is a known neuropsychiatric risk agent that can potentiate serotonergic effects and CNS toxicity when combined with paroxetine (SSRI), increasing risk of serotonin syndrome, seizures, and severe psychiatric adverse effects.
action: Avoid this combination if possible; if mefloquine is unavoidably required for malaria prophylaxis, use alternative antimalarials (atovaquone-proguanil or doxycycline) or consider switching to non-serotonergic antidepressants.
